doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Pause, his deep voice and remembering Joe Williams
summary: A break for sound, jokes about his voice and Rowe's first phone call to him, with a mention of Joe.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: All right. We’re going to take a pause here for a moment. Apparently we have a little—
Yeah, my voice is too loud I’m afraid. I’m sorry.
And that’s why there’s never a question about who’s on the telephone. TH: People listen when you talk.

Do you remember — I remember this distinctly — the first time I ever talked to you when this whole thing came up, I had the meeting with Mary Kopcza and the whole thing, and then I called you and I said, “Mr. Fillius? This is Monk Rowe and I’m calling from Hamilton College.” And you said, “I’ve heard of it.” I’ll never forget that. I’ll also never forget the first time I called Joe and that voice over the phone, it was so rich and low that it was really —
Well we’ll talk about him too.
People never knew that he was a great philosopher. I mean it’s totally aside from his talent. He really —
